summary: Martin Delhey specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and also studied at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Hamburg, Göttingen, Ryukoku University, Shandong University, and IIBS.
Martin Gusinde studied at the University of Vienna from around 1924 to 1927. He later held an academic post at the Catholic University of America from approximately 1949 to 1957.

Martin Haug was a scholar of Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. Educated at Tübingen, Göttingen, and Bonn under Roth, Benfey, and Ewald, he served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College and the University of Munich.

Philosopher Martin Heidegger studied at the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Rickert and Edmund Husserl. He held academic posts at Freiburg (1915–1923, 1936–1940) and the University of Marburg (1923–1928).

Martin Joachim Kümmel is a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He completed his MA, PhD, and habilitation at the University of Freiburg, where he served until 2008, before becoming chairholder at Jena in 2013.

Martin Johannes Hammerich was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. Educated at the University of Copenhagen, he studied under A. W. von Schlegel and H. H. Wilson, later serving as docent in Sanskrit at Copenhagen and principal of Borgerdydskolen i Christianshavn.

Martin King Whyte is a sociologist and sinologist who studied at Cornell and Harvard. He held posts at Boston University, the University of Michigan (1970–1994), George Washington University, and Harvard University, where he became professor emeritus in 2000.
Martin Kraatz is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He completed his doctoral studies under Wilhelm Rau and succeeded Käthe Neumann in 1968.

Martin Lehnert works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. After earning his PhD at the University of Freiburg, he served as Professor of East Asian Religion and Philosophy at the University of Munich, attested in 2016.

Martin Lowenthal works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche and Namkhai Norbu, and held posts at Boston College and Harvard University.

Martin Mills is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Edinburgh in 1997. He taught at the University of Sussex before joining the University of Aberdeen, where he was appointed Chair in 2024.
Martin Novosad was a Buddhist studies figure who studied as a disciple under Nyanatiloka Mahathera in 1938. In 1940, he served as leader at the Verdant Hermitage.

Sociologist of religion Martin Riesebrodt studied at Tübingen, Humboldt, Heidelberg (Promotion), and Munich (Habilitation). He served as professor at the University of Chicago from 1990 to 2011 and at the Graduate Institute of International and Development Studies in 2013.

Martin Schultze was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1855. He served as Director at Höhere Töchterschule in Cüstrin (1869–1877) and Rector at Theodor-Mommsen-Schule (1877–1885).

Martin Seeger works in Buddhist studies. He completed his PhD at the University of Hamburg under Barend Jan Terwiel by 2004, held a post at Hamburg, and serves as a Council Member of the Pali Text Society.

Martin Straube is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Michael Hahn. His affiliations attested in 2026 include posts at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, the University of Bristol, and Savitribai Phule Pune University.

Martin T. Adam works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned his PhD at McGill University under Richard P. Hayes and studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, later serving as an instructor at McGill.

Martin Williams earned an MA at Keele University (1972–1979). He worked as an IT Adviser for Powys County Council (1989–2007) and served as Co-ordinator for the Naga Conciliation Group with the Religious Society of Friends (2011–2014).

Martin Willson worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers including Thubten Yeshe, Thubten Zopa Rinpoche, Geshe Thubten Loden, Zasep Tulku Rinpoche, Geshe Rabten, Geshe Jampa Tegchok, and Geshe Lhundup Sopa.

Martina Draszczyk is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Lambert Schmithausen and earned her Dr.phil. at the University of Vienna, later serving as Numata Professor at Vienna (2021) and McGill University (2022).
